passages.text: All three belong to the amide class. Their central nervous system (CNS) and cardiovascular toxicities are additive when used in combination.
Where combination use is indicated, the Loewe dose-additivity principle applies: (Dose A ÷ MRD A) + (Dose B ÷ MRD B) ≤ 1.0
If a third agent is used, its fractional contribution is added to the sum. Vasoconstrictor content must be audited independently of this calculation.
Clinically significant discrepancies between guideline sources for maximum recommended dosages (MRDs) persist
Up to 40% of LAST cases present atypically, with delayed onset, cardiovascular signs preceding neurological features, or both systems affected simultaneously.
Vigilance must be maintained for at least 30 min post-injection.
Vasovagal syncope | Seconds–minutes | Dizziness; nausea; pallor; brief loss of consciousness | Bradycardia; hypotension | Anxiety/pain trigger; rapid recovery supine; no metallic taste or seizure

Adrenaline/sympathomimetic reaction | 30–60 s | Anxiety; tremor; headache; palpitation sensation | Tachycardia; palpitations; hypertension | Self-resolving; no CNS toxicity progression; tachycardia, not bradycardia

Concurrent benzodiazepine or opioid sedation may mask early CNS LAST symptoms (tinnitus, agitation, confusion), eliminating the neurological warning window before cardiovascular deterioration—enhanced monitoring of all vital parameters is essential in sedated patients.
Reduced protein binding increases the free fraction of all LA agents; most relevant for bupivacaine (95% protein-bound) in liver disease, nephrotic syndrome, malnutrition, and critical illness.

Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) potentiate bupivacaine’s negative inotropy, with EC50 potentiation factors of 1.4–3.3 across agents. This pharmacodynamic interaction does not alter the fractional dose calculation

The fractional dose rule is a pharmacologically justified safety heuristic with acknowledged pharmacokinetic limitations. ILE is a specific rescue therapy for severe or cardiovascular LAST; airway support and oxygenation remain the primary interventions.
The fractional dose rule must be applied when combining amide local anaesthetics; failure to do so is a recognised clinical error.

passages.text: FHdRCC is a rare and aggressive subtype of type 2 papillary RCC, mainly affecting younger patients, metastazing early from small solitary lesions. It is caused by an inactivating mutation of the FH gene
The more general term FHdRCC should rather be used to include both hereditary and known sporadic forms of cancer development.

FHdRCC can be associated with the hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC) syndrome, an autosomal-dominant hereditable syndrome with predisposition to develop smooth muscle tumors of the skin and uterus.

FH deficiency results in the accumulation of fumarate, which in turn leads to activation of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) through inhibition of prolyl hydroxylases. HIF promotes tumorigenesis by orchestrating a metabolic switch to glycolysis even under normoxia

Fumarate and its immediate precursor succinate can act as oncometabolites by competitively inhibiting α-ketoglutarate (α-KG)-dependent dioxygenases, a family of enzymes that also includes prolyl hydroxylases.
Of note, glutamine replenishment of the TCA cycle can result in fumarate accumulation even in FH-containing cells
Yet, it still remains difficult to distinguish FHdRCC from papillary RCC by means of solely pathological criteria.
Accumulating fumarate and succinate for instance suppress histone and DNA demethylases by depletion of α-KG causing genome-wide epigenetic modifications that further contribute to tumorigenesis

In cancer cells with FH deficiency, fumarate can also react with cysteine residues of proteins in a non-enzymatic manner, generating S-(2-succinyl)cysteine. Such a protein modification, which is known as cysteine succination, eliminates the ability of Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1) to repress nuclear factor (erythroid-derived 2)-like 2 (NRF2)

passages.text: In dogs, the MDR1 nt230(del4) 4-base pair (4-bp) deletion in exon 4 of the MDR1 gene (syn. MDR1-1Δ or ABCB1-1Δ) leads to an early stop codon already at amino acid position 91 of the 1281 amino acid spanning wild-type MDR1 carrier protein. In cats, the MDR1 nt1930(del2) 2-bp deletion in exon 15 of the MDR1 gene (syn. ABCB1 1930_1931del TC) truncates the wild-type cat MDR1 protein of 1279 amino acids to its first half representing amino acids 1–643.
The present study found an allelic frequency of 0.625% for the MDR1 mutation in 800 cats from Germany.

In both cell lines, significant MDR1-mediated rhodamine 123 efflux was identified for the wild-type MDR1 proteins, but not for the mutant MDR1 proteins, confirming a complete loss-of-function phenotype due to MDR1 gene mutation.

Competitive in vitro studies showed inhibition of both wild-type MDR1 carriers with the reference MDR1 inhibitors verapamil, PSC833, and tariquidar, as well as with the antiparasitic drugs ivermectin, eprinomectin, moxidectin, selamectin, lotilaner, and sarolaner
At the blood–brain barrier, MDR1 restricts brain entry of potentially neurotoxic drugs, such as ivermectin.

passages.text: However, quantification of the effect of the interacting drug on warfarin dose is complicated and varies based on the interacting medication, genetic variants affecting the responsible metabolizing enzyme and other inter-individual variations.

The table generally accounts for clinical factors (e.g., age, weight, sex, race, concomitant drugs, and comorbidities) but doesn’t account for other genetic variants that may affect warfarin maintenance dose variability. The second approach is through the use of pharmacogenetic algorithms, which often include genetic components in addition to clinical factors.
Genetic dosing uses patients’ genetic test results to predict the initial warfarin dose.
